breakfast.name: Cinnamon Roll Croissants (Flaky Layered Rolls with Cream Cheese Glaze)
ingredients: CREAM CHEESE GLAZE: 4 oz cream cheese softened, 1 cup powdered sugar, 2 tbsp milk, 1/2 tsp vanilla
instructions: Roll the puff pastry out on a floured surface into a large rectangle, about 10x14 inches.
Spread the softened butter evenly across the entire surface.
Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg together, then sprinkle the mixture over the buttered pastry.
Starting from the long edge, roll the pastry up tightly into a log.
Slice the log into 8 even rounds and place them cut-side up on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving space between each one.
Brush the tops with beaten egg wash.
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes until the layers are golden, puffed, and flaky.
While they bake, beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla until smooth.
Drizzle the cream cheese glaze generously over the warm croissants and serve immediately.
breakfast.description: The buttery, flaky layers of a croissant meet the warm cinnamon-sugar swirl of a classic cinnamon roll. Puff pastry makes this mashup surprisingly easy — roll, fill, slice, and bake until golden, then finish with a tangy cream cheese glaze.

breakfast.name: Cinnamon Roll Focaccia
ingredients: CINNAMON SWIRL: 1/3 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon
GLAZE: 1 cup powdered sugar, 2 tbsp milk, 1/2 tsp vanilla
instructions: Stir together the warm water, yeast, and 1 tbsp of the sugar. Let it sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour, remaining sugar, olive oil, and salt. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Oil a 9x13-inch baking pan. Press the risen dough into the pan, stretching it to fill the corners.
Mix the softened butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon into a paste. Drop spoonfuls across the top of the dough.
Use your fingertips to dimple the dough deeply in the classic focaccia style, pressing the cinnamon-sugar mixture down into the dimples so it pools and swirls.
Let rest 20 minutes while the oven heats to 375°F.
Bake 22-25 minutes until golden on top and cooked through.
Whisk the powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla together and drizzle over the warm focaccia.
Tear into pieces and serve warm.
breakfast.description: Focaccia's pillowy, olive-oil dough meets cinnamon roll filling — the deep dimples trap pools of melted brown sugar and cinnamon butter. Drizzled with vanilla glaze, it tears apart into the best breakfast bread you've ever had.

dinner.name: Dumpling Lasagna
ingredients: TOPPING: extra chili oil, sesame seeds, sliced green onions
instructions: Mix the lamb mince, sliced green onions, minced garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, chili oil, white pepper, and chicken stock together in a bowl until well combined.
Line the bottom of a heatproof dish or steamer basket with a single layer of dumpling wrappers, overlapping them slightly like lasagna sheets.
Spread a thin, even layer of the lamb filling over the wrappers.
Add another layer of dumpling wrappers on top, then another layer of filling.
Repeat for 3-4 layers total, ending with a layer of wrappers on top.
Steam the assembled lasagna for 20-25 minutes until the wrappers are silky and translucent and the lamb is cooked through.
Finish with a generous drizzle of chili oil, a scatter of sesame seeds, and sliced green onions.
Slice and serve straight from the dish.
dinner.description: Lasagna reimagined through Chinese dumpling flavors — layers of silky dumpling wrappers replace pasta sheets, with a savory lamb filling seasoned with soy, sesame, and garlic. Steamed instead of baked, the wrappers turn translucent and tender.

snacks.name: Classic Dark Chocolate Shortbread with Sea Salt
ingredients: 1 cup (250 ml) unsalted butter, at room temperature
300g (10.5 oz) dark chocolate (70% cacao), broken into squares
Maldon sea salt or flaky sea salt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.
Using an electric mixer, cream together the butter, brown sugar, and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Add the flour 1/2 cup at a time, mixing until all flour is incorporated and the dough forms a ball.
Cover and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough out until about 1 cm (3/8 inch) thick.
Cut into 24 rectangles. Transfer to the prepared baking sheets, spacing them 1 inch apart.
Top each cookie with 1 square of dark chocolate.
Bake in batches for 12-15 minutes or just until the cookies begin to brown.
Cool for 2 minutes, then sprinkle lightly with flaky sea salt.
Cool completely on the baking sheets before transferring to an airtight container.
snacks.description: Buttery, crumbly shortbread topped with a square of premium dark chocolate that melts slightly in the oven, finished with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. The three textures — sandy cookie, smooth chocolate, crunchy salt — are pure indulgence.

desserts.name: Tiramisu Brownies
ingredients: BROWNIE LAYER: 1/2 cup melted butter, 1 cup sugar, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup cocoa powder, 3/4 cup flour, pinch of salt
2 tbsp brewed espresso or strong coffee (mixed into brownie batter)
MASCARPONE LAYER: 8 oz mascarpone cheese, 1/4 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 egg yolk
TOPPING: cocoa powder for dusting, chocolate shavings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a square baking pan.
Stir the melted butter and sugar together until smooth.
Add the eggs and espresso and mix until the batter is glossy.
Fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt until no dry streaks remain.
Pour about two-thirds of the brownie batter into the pan and spread it flat.
Beat the mascarpone with the powdered sugar, vanilla, and egg yolk until smooth and creamy.
Dollop the mascarpone mixture over the brownie layer and spread it gently.
Spoon the remaining brownie batter on top and use a knife to swirl it through the mascarpone for a marbled effect.
Bake for 25 minutes until the edges are set but the center still has a slight wobble.
Cool completely, then dust generously with cocoa powder and top with chocolate shavings.
Chill for at least 1 hour before slicing for the cleanest cuts.
desserts.description: Rich espresso-laced brownies swirled with creamy mascarpone and dusted with cocoa — all the flavors of tiramisu baked into a fudgy, sliceable bar. The mascarpone layer stays creamy against the dense chocolate.

desserts.name: Salted Caramel Cheesecake (Creamy No-Bake)
ingredients: CRUST: 2 cups graham cracker crumbs, 6 tbsp melted butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar
FILLING: 16 oz (2 blocks) cream cheese softened, 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 cup heavy whipping cream
CARAMEL: 1/2 cup store-bought salted caramel sauce (or homemade)
TOPPING: extra caramel sauce, flaky sea salt, whipped cream
instructions: Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and brown sugar. Press firmly into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
Refrigerate the crust while you make the filling.
Beat the softened cream cheese until completely smooth with no lumps.
Add the powdered sugar and vanilla, beating until combined.
In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream to stiff peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the cream cheese mixture gently until no streaks remain.
Pour half the filling over the crust and smooth it out.
Drizzle the salted caramel sauce over the filling in a swirl pattern.
Add the remaining filling on top and smooth the surface.
Drizzle more caramel on top and use a knife to create a marble pattern.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight for the best set.
Before serving, top with a final drizzle of caramel and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt.
desserts.description: A creamy no-bake cheesecake with ribbons of salted caramel swirled through a cloud-light cream cheese filling on a buttery graham cracker crust. No oven required — just patience while it sets in the fridge.

desserts.name: Japanese Coffee Jelly
ingredients: 3 tbsp cold water (to bloom the gelatin)
FOR SERVING (choose one): sweetened cream, sweetened condensed milk, half & half, whipped cream, or vanilla ice cream
instructions: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let it sit for 5 minutes to bloom.
Microwave the bloomed gelatin for 30 seconds or until fully dissolved.
Brew the coffee strong. Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Add the dissolved gelatin to the hot coffee and stir well to combine.
Pour into a shallow baking dish or pan.
Refrigerate for 4-5 hours or until the jelly is fully set and firm.
Once set, cut the coffee jelly into cubes or use small cookie cutters for fun shapes.
Divide the cubes among serving glasses or bowls.
Pour your choice of cream, condensed milk, or half & half over the jelly cubes.
Serve chilled — add ice if you want to eat it right away, though it will dilute the sweetness slightly.
desserts.description: A beloved Japanese kissaten (coffee shop) dessert — strong coffee set into wobbly, bittersweet jelly cubes, then bathed in sweetened cream. The contrast of bitter coffee and sweet cream is addictive, and the bouncy texture is unlike any Western dessert.

desserts.name: Thai Tea Crème Brûlée
ingredients: TOPPING: 2-3 tbsp granulated sugar for torching
instructions: In a saucepan, combine the heavy cream and milk. Heat on low just until the mixture begins to simmer — do not boil.
Turn off the heat and add the Thai tea mix. Steep for 15 minutes so the cream turns a deep orange and absorbs the tea's flavor.
Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla paste until combined. Set aside.
Strain the infused cream through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the tea leaves. Reheat the cream on low until it just simmers again.
While whisking constantly, very slowly drizzle the hot cream into the egg yolk mixture to temper it without curdling.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup with a pouring lip.
Divide the mixture among 4 ramekins (3 inches / 7.5 cm diameter). Skim off any foam and pop any air bubbles.
Place the ramekins in a baking pan. Pour boiling water into the pan until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake 35-40 minutes until the custard is set but still has a slight wobble in the center.
Remove from the water bath. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours (or up to 3 days).
When ready to serve, sprinkle 1 1/2 to 2 tsp sugar evenly on each custard.
Torch the sugar in a circular pattern until it caramelizes to a deep amber. Let the sugar cool and harden for 30 seconds before serving.
desserts.description: Classic French crème brûlée infused with the distinctive sweet, spiced, and creamy flavor of Thai iced tea. The orange-tinted custard cracks through a thin shell of caramelized sugar — a collision of two iconic dessert traditions.

drinks.name: Caramel Apple Chai (with Cinnamon Maple Cold Foam)
ingredients: Caramel sauce (cajeta or store-bought) for lining the cup
Cinnamon maple cold foam (store-bought or homemade: 1/4 cup cold milk frothed with 1 tsp maple syrup and 1/4 tsp cinnamon)
instructions: Steep 3 chai tea bags in 1/2 cup of hot water for 5 minutes to make a strong chai concentrate. Remove the bags and let the concentrate cool slightly.
Drizzle caramel sauce (cajeta works beautifully) around the inside walls of your serving glass.
Stir the apple butter into the warm chai concentrate until fully dissolved.
Fill the glass with ice.
Pour the apple-butter chai over the ice.
Add milk or cream of your choice to fill the glass about three-quarters.
Top with cinnamon maple cold foam — to make your own, froth cold milk with maple syrup and a pinch of cinnamon until thick and foamy.
Sip through the foam layer and enjoy the fall-in-a-cup vibes.
drinks.description: A cozy autumn drink that layers spiced chai with apple butter sweetness, caramel-lined glass walls, and a crown of cinnamon maple cold foam. Like apple pie and a chai latte had the most seasonal baby possible.
